adapter_hint: INSTAT RGPH5 2022 thematic report on cultural characteristics (religion, ethnie, langue maternelle) by region, its 20 regions summed into the 9 shapes: python -m scripts.fetch_census.mali
language_note: INSTAT Mali, 5ème Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGPH5, 2022), rapport thématique Caractéristiques culturelles de la population. Annex Tableau 6: langue maternelle as the census groups it, of the 19.1 million people the table covers against a resident population of 21.3 million; the report does not state the table's age floor. Sonrhai/Songhoy/Zarma is shown as Sonrhai/Djerma and Sarakole/Sooninke as Maraka/Soninke. The report prints each region's shares to two decimals and its population, and the counts here are the one applied to the other. The region as drawn here is the report's regions of Gao and Ménaka of 2023, added together.
religion_note: INSTAT Mali, 5ème Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGPH5, 2022), rapport thématique Caractéristiques culturelles de la population. Tableau 2.03: the resident population by religion as the census asks it (Musulman, Chrétien, Animiste, Sans religion, Autre religion). The report prints each region's shares to two decimals and its population, and the counts here are the one applied to the other. The region as drawn here is the report's regions of Gao and Ménaka of 2023, added together.
ethnicity_note: INSTAT Mali, 5ème Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGPH5, 2022), rapport thématique Caractéristiques culturelles de la population. Annex Tableau 5: the 22 ethnies the census names, of the Malian population (the report's Autre ethnie non malienne is kept as a group; foreign nationals are outside the table). Bamanan/Bambara is shown as Bambara, Peulh as Fula, Souraka/Maure as Moor, Tamasheq/Touareg as Tuareg. The report prints each region's shares to two decimals and its population, and the counts here are the one applied to the other. The region as drawn here is the report's regions of Gao and Ménaka of 2023, added together.
population_note: The 2022 census counts the region as drawn here as the regions of 2023 made from it: Gao 727,517 and Ménaka 318,876 (Tableau 2.3), added here. Its 4 divisions drawn on this map add up to 668,410 (OCHA's common operational dataset, 2018), 36% below this figure.
median_age_note: Interpolated within the five-year age group that holds the middle person, from the 2022 census's count of the population of ordinary households by five-year age group (Tableaux A.02 to A.21), of the regions of Gao and Ménaka of 2023 together.

language_note: The 2009 census's principal language of the region's residents aged 6 and over (Tableau S-3, as the US Census Bureau tabulates it); children under six were not asked. The 2022 census tabulates mother tongue for the regions of 2023, and their lines cross this region's: the Bougouni region of 2023 took in the cercle of Ouélessébougou and part of the cercle of Sélingué from Koulikoro, and the Koutiala region of 2023 part of the cercle of Bla from Ségou.
religion_note: Afrobarometer Round 9, a nationally representative sample of citizens of voting age. Regional shares are survey estimates, not census counts: they carry sampling error, and regions with fewer than 25 respondents are omitted rather than estimated. This region: 224 respondents.
ethnicity_note: Afrobarometer Round 9, a nationally representative sample of citizens of voting age. Regional shares are survey estimates, not census counts: they carry sampling error, and regions with fewer than 25 respondents are omitted rather than estimated. This region: 224 respondents.
population_note: The sum of all 7 divisions drawn inside it, which all carry figures for 2018 from OCHA's common operational dataset. It replaces 2,643,179 for 2009, an older figure from Institut National de la Statistique.
median_age_note: The 2009 census's count of the region as drawn here, as it stood before 2023, by five-year age group: the median is interpolated within the group holding the middle person. The 2022 census counts the regions of 2023, and their lines cross this region's: the Bougouni region of 2023 took in the cercle of Ouélessébougou and part of the cercle of Sélingué from Koulikoro, and the Koutiala region of 2023 part of the cercle of Bla from Ségou.
sex_ratio_note: The 2009 census's count of the region as drawn here, as it stood before 2023: 1,303,903 men and 1,339,276 women. The 2022 census counts the regions of 2023, and their lines cross this region's: the Bougouni region of 2023 took in the cercle of Ouélessébougou and part of the cercle of Sélingué from Koulikoro, and the Koutiala region of 2023 part of the cercle of Bla from Ségou.

adapter_hint: INSTAT RGPH5 2022 thematic report on cultural characteristics (religion, ethnie, langue maternelle) by region, its 20 regions summed into the 9 shapes: python -m scripts.fetch_census.mali
language_note: INSTAT Mali, 5ème Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGPH5, 2022), rapport thématique Caractéristiques culturelles de la population. Annex Tableau 6: langue maternelle as the census groups it, of the 19.1 million people the table covers against a resident population of 21.3 million; the report does not state the table's age floor. Sonrhai/Songhoy/Zarma is shown as Sonrhai/Djerma and Sarakole/Sooninke as Maraka/Soninke. The report prints each region's shares to two decimals and its population, and the counts here are the one applied to the other. The region as drawn here is the report's regions of Tombouctou and Taoudenni of 2023, added together.
religion_note: INSTAT Mali, 5ème Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGPH5, 2022), rapport thématique Caractéristiques culturelles de la population. Tableau 2.03: the resident population by religion as the census asks it (Musulman, Chrétien, Animiste, Sans religion, Autre religion). The report prints each region's shares to two decimals and its population, and the counts here are the one applied to the other. The region as drawn here is the report's regions of Tombouctou and Taoudenni of 2023, added together.
ethnicity_note: INSTAT Mali, 5ème Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGPH5, 2022), rapport thématique Caractéristiques culturelles de la population. Annex Tableau 5: the 22 ethnies the census names, of the Malian population (the report's Autre ethnie non malienne is kept as a group; foreign nationals are outside the table). Bamanan/Bambara is shown as Bambara, Peulh as Fula, Souraka/Maure as Moor, Tamasheq/Touareg as Tuareg. The report prints each region's shares to two decimals and its population, and the counts here are the one applied to the other. The region as drawn here is the report's regions of Tombouctou and Taoudenni of 2023, added together.
population_note: The 2022 census counts the region as drawn here as the regions of 2023 made from it: Tombouctou 974,278 and Taoudenni 100,358 (Tableau 2.3), added here. Its 5 divisions drawn on this map add up to 831,707 (OCHA's common operational dataset, 2018), 23% below this figure.
median_age_note: Interpolated within the five-year age group that holds the middle person, from the 2022 census's count of the population of ordinary households by five-year age group (Tableaux A.02 to A.21), of the regions of Tombouctou and Taoudenni of 2023 together.
